strongest_angle: The legal battle centers on whether Michael Mann's screenplay for the 1995 film Heat qualifies as a work-for-hire, which would prevent the director from reclaiming copyright ownership under Section 203 of the Copyright Act.

key_facts.fact: New Regency filed a lawsuit in the United States District Court for the Central District of California to block Michael Mann from reclaiming the copyright to the 1995 film Heat.
key_facts.source_name: United States District Court Central District of California

key_facts.fact: Michael Mann served three separate termination notices to New Regency in 2026, attempting to invoke Section 203(a) of the Copyright Act to regain screenplay rights.
New Regency, led by Yariv Milchan, argues that the screenplay is a work-for-hire, which would legally exempt the work from the copyright termination provisions Mann is attempting to use.
Michael Mann is scheduled to begin filming the sequel Heat 2 in January 2027, creating a deadline for the resolution of the ownership dispute over the original 1995 property.
